sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: A plane goes down somewhere in the Pacific.
sentences.zh: 一架飞机在太平洋某处坠毁了。

sentences.en: The survivors, stranded on a deserted island, are a group of schoolboys.
sentences.zh: 幸存者被困在一个荒岛上，是一群男学生。

sentences.en: At first, they celebrate their newfound escape from adult supervision, playing on the beach.
sentences.zh: 起初，他们庆祝自己摆脱了大人的管束，在海滩上嬉戏。

sentences.en: Then they organize.
sentences.zh: 接着他们组织起来。

sentences.en: They elect one of the boys, Ralph, as their chief.
sentences.zh: 他们选举其中一个男孩拉尔夫为首领。

sentences.en: Ralph and several others get a fire going.
sentences.zh: 拉尔夫和其他几个人生起了火。

sentences.en: But soon the boys begin resisting Ralph's efforts to lead them.
sentences.zh: 但很快，男孩们开始抗拒拉尔夫领导他们的努力。

sentences.en: The boys assigned to watch over the fire get distracted, and the fire goes out.
sentences.zh: 负责看守火堆的男孩们分心了，火熄灭了。

sentences.en: They become paranoid and stoke each other's fears of a beast they're convinced is stalking the island.
sentences.zh: 他们变得多疑，并且煽动彼此对一头野兽的恐惧，他们坚信那头野兽正在岛上游荡。

sentences.en: They split into warring factions and begin attacking one another.
sentences.zh: 他们分裂成交战的派别，开始互相攻击。

sentences.en: Three of them die.
sentences.zh: 其中三人死了。

sentences.en: This is the story told in the 1954 novel, Lord of the Flies.
sentences.zh: 这就是1954年出版的小说《蝇王》中讲述的故事。

sentences.en: It was written by an English schoolteacher named William Golding,
sentences.zh: 它是由一位名叫威廉·戈尔丁的英国男教师写的，

sentences.en: and it reflected his harsh view of humans in general, and children in particular.
sentences.zh: 它反映了他对总的人类、特别是儿童的严苛看法。

sentences.en: The novel ends when a British naval officer lands on the island and finds the children in a ragged, feral state.
sentences.zh: 小说的结局是一名英国海军军官登陆小岛，发现孩子们处于衣衫褴褛、野蛮的状态。

sentences.en: The novel entered the cultural consciousness as a warning.
sentences.zh: 这部小说作为一个警示进入了文化意识中。

sentences.en: Without rules, systems, and adult supervision, children left alone would descend into chaos.
sentences.zh: 如果没有规则、制度和成人的监督，独自留下的儿童将会陷入混乱。

sentences.en: As with many generalizations, there is some truth to this.
sentences.zh: 就像许多概括一样，这有一定的道理。

sentences.en: A multitude of studies suggest kids thrive when they have stability.
sentences.zh: 大量研究表明，当孩子拥有稳定性时，他们会茁壮成长。

sentences.en: Chaotic and unpredictable environments can bring out the worst in us.
sentences.zh: 混乱和不可预测的环境会激发出我们最不好的一面。

sentences.en: But today we explore whether many societies have taken William Golding's warning too much to heart.
sentences.zh: 但今天我们要探讨的是，许多社会是否把威廉·戈尔丁的警告太当回事了。

sentences.en: If some supervision of children is a good thing, lots of parents, teachers, and school administrators seem to think
sentences.zh: 如果对孩子的适度监管是件好事，许多父母、老师和学校管理者似乎认为

sentences.en: more is always better.
sentences.zh: 越多总是越好。

sentences.en: When more is less, and less is more, this week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 当多即是少，少即是多，本周的《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: When you're first learning to swim, it's not a good idea to be pushed into very deep water.
sentences.zh: 当你刚开始学游泳时，被推到很深的水里并不是个好主意。

sentences.en: You could drown.
sentences.zh: 你可能会淹死。

sentences.en: But it's also not a very good idea to simply waddle around in the shallow.
sentences.zh: 但只是在浅水区蹚来蹚去也不是个好主意。

sentences.en: You'll never learn to swim.
sentences.zh: 你永远也学不会游泳。

sentences.en: If you're a parent or a teacher, you're constantly asking yourself how to balance risk and safety for the kids in your care.
sentences.zh: 如果你是父母或老师，你经常会问自己，如何在照顾的孩子身上平衡风险和安全。

sentences.en: Tip too far in one direction, and you can put children in danger.
sentences.zh: 向一个方向倾斜太多，你就会让儿童陷入危险。

sentences.en: Go too far in the other, and you deprive kids of the joy and power of exploration.
sentences.zh: 向另一个方向走得太远，你就会剥夺儿童探索的快乐和力量。

sentences.en: At Boston College, psychologist Peter Gray studies how the balance between exploration and safety
sentences.zh: 在波士顿学院，心理学家彼得·格雷研究了探索与安全之间的平衡

sentences.en: has changed for many children, and the effects this has on their minds.
sentences.zh: 对许多儿童发生了怎样的变化，以及这对他们的思想产生的影响。

sentences.en: Peter Gray, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 彼得·格雷，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm very happy to be here.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Peter, you were once at a pop-up event where the organizers provided kids with various materials,
sentences.zh: 彼得，你曾经参加过一个快闪活动，组织者为孩子们提供了各种材料，

sentences.en: including twigs and tree branches, old boards, hammers, nails.
sentences.zh: 包括细枝和树枝、旧木板、锤子、钉子。

sentences.en: Paint me a picture of the scene and tell me what happened.
sentences.zh: 请给我描绘一下当时的场景，并告诉我发生了什么。

sentences.en: Yeah, so there were two young children, maybe around six years old,
sentences.zh: 是的，当时有两个小孩，大概六岁左右，

sentences.en: very happily taking a couple of some of the very narrow boards and laying them out on the grass
sentences.zh: 非常高兴地拿着几块非常窄的木板，把它们铺在草地上，

sentences.en: and walking along them like they were walking on a tightrope
sentences.zh: 并沿着它们走，就像走钢丝一样，

sentences.en: and pretending that this was a very narrow bridge and there were crocodiles on either side.
sentences.zh: 假装这是一座非常窄的桥，两边都是鳄鱼。

sentences.en: And it was a very imaginative game.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极富想象力的游戏。

sentences.en: They were clearly having a lot of fun, and the dad, I assume it was the dad,
sentences.zh: 他们显然玩得很开心，父亲——我猜那是父亲，

sentences.en: at least of one of the two, came over and said,
sentences.zh: 至少是其中一个孩子的父亲——走了过来，说：

sentences.en: that's not what you're supposed to do with the boards.
sentences.zh: 木板可不是这么用的。

sentences.en: We're supposed to be building something with the boards.
sentences.zh: 我们应该用木板建造点东西。

sentences.en: See, there's hammer and nails here.
sentences.zh: 看，这里有锤子和钉子。

sentences.en: And then he proceeded to take the boards
sentences.zh: 接着他开始拿起木板，

sentences.en: and to start showing the children how to pound with hammer and nails.
sentences.zh: 并开始向孩子们展示如何用锤子和钉子敲打。

sentences.en: And what I observed is the children suddenly changed from really very happy and playful
sentences.zh: 我观察到的是，孩子们突然从非常快乐和顽皮的状态，

sentences.en: to quite bored as they watched their father show them how to pound nails into boards.
sentences.zh: 变得相当无聊，因为他们看着父亲向他们展示如何把钉子敲进木板。

sentences.en: There was another time, Peter, when a sixth grade teacher told you about a game
sentences.zh: 还有一次，彼得，有一位六年级老师向你讲述了一个游戏，

sentences.en: that her students had invented during the COVID pandemic.
sentences.zh: 是她的学生在新冠大流行期间发明的。

sentences.en: What was this game?
sentences.zh: 这是个什么游戏？

sentences.en: She was feeling very bad for her sixth graders.
sentences.zh: 她对她的六年级学生感到非常抱歉。

sentences.en: They're still children, really.
sentences.zh: 他们其实还是孩子。

sentences.en: You know, they're 11 and 12 years old at most, and they're indoors all the school day.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们最多11、12岁，一整天上学都在室内。

sentences.en: They don't have any recess at all.
sentences.zh: 他们根本没有任何课间休息。

sentences.en: So she thought, well, wouldn't it be nice if I at least gave them a half an hour to play
sentences.zh: 所以她想，好吧，如果我至少让他们在上学前有半个小时的时间玩耍，

sentences.en: before school starts?
sentences.zh: 那不是很好吗？

sentences.en: Some of them arrived early anyway.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，他们中的一些人来得很早。

sentences.en: And it turns out they arrived eagerly early when she provided that play opportunity.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，当她提供这个玩耍的机会时，他们都急切地早到了。

sentences.en: So she let them play in the ways that they wanted to play.
sentences.zh: 所以她让他们以自己想要的方式玩耍。

sentences.en: And one of the games that they played, this was after COVID,
sentences.zh: 他们玩的游戏之一，这是在新冠之后，

sentences.en: was called something like infection, or maybe it was called COVID, something like that.
sentences.zh: 叫做“感染”之类的，或者可能叫“新冠”，诸如此类的名字。

sentences.en: And some of the children were infection.
sentences.zh: 有些孩子是感染者。

sentences.en: And if they touched somebody, you became infected and might die.
sentences.zh: 如果他们碰了某个人，你就被感染了，可能会死。

sentences.en: And others were called vaccine.
sentences.zh: 其他人被称为疫苗。

sentences.en: And they could prevent you from dying by coming and touching you.
sentences.zh: 他们可以通过过来触摸你来阻止你死去。

sentences.en: It was quite an imaginative game.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很有想象力的游戏。

sentences.en: I have no idea how they developed, but the teacher said they were clearly having a lot
sentences.zh: 我不知道他们是怎么开发出来的，但老师说他们显然玩得

sentences.en: of fun with that.
sentences.zh: 非常开心。

sentences.en: But then one of the school administrators observed that, and she said, no, we can't have games
sentences.zh: 但后来学校的一位管理者看到了那一幕，她说，不，我们不能进行

sentences.en: like that going on.
sentences.zh: 这样的游戏。

sentences.en: We can't have people pretending to die.
sentences.zh: 我们不能让人们假装死去。

sentences.en: I've heard of many stories where recesses have been very much curtailed and limited because
sentences.zh: 我听说过许多关于课间休息因关于玩耍中能做什么和不能做什么的规则而大大缩减和限制的故事。

sentences.en: of rules about what you can and cannot do in play.
sentences.zh: 关于玩耍中能做什么和不能做什么的规则。

sentences.en: Peter noticed something similar in his own life.
sentences.zh: 彼得在自己的生活中也注意到了类似的事情。

sentences.en: When his son was little, both of them took part in something called a Pinewood Derby.
sentences.zh: 当他的儿子还小的时候，他们两个都参加了一个叫松木车德比的活动。

sentences.en: Yeah, so this was designed to promote bonding between fathers and their sons.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是为了促进父亲和儿子之间的感情。

sentences.en: And the boys were about eight years old at this time.
sentences.zh: 当时男孩们大约八岁。

sentences.en: And the way it works is each father-son pair is given a kit that includes a piece of very
sentences.zh: 它的运作方式是，给每对父子发一个工具包，其中包括一块非常软的松木，

sentences.en: soft pine wood, about seven inches long, and wheels that can be attached to it.
sentences.zh: 大约七英寸长，以及可以附着在上面的轮子。

sentences.en: And the idea is to carve the wood into something that looks like a race car and to attach the
sentences.zh: 这个想法是将木头雕刻成看起来像赛车的东西，并装上

sentences.en: wheels.
sentences.zh: 轮子。

sentences.en: And then everybody brings them back to the next meeting of the group and you race them down
sentences.zh: 然后每个人把它们带回小组的下一次聚会，你把它们放在

sentences.en: a slope.
sentences.zh: 斜坡上比赛。

sentences.en: So my interpretation of this was this was an opportunity for children to do something a
sentences.zh: 所以我对此的理解是，这是一个让孩子们做一些

sentences.en: little bit risky, using a knife to carve the soft wood and for fathers to help out.
sentences.zh: 有点冒险的事情的机会，用刀雕刻软木头，让父亲们帮忙。

sentences.en: And that's the way we did it.
sentences.zh: 我们就是这么做的。

sentences.en: And I was very proud of it.
sentences.zh: 我为此感到非常自豪。

sentences.en: He was proud of it.
sentences.zh: 他为此感到骄傲。

sentences.en: He painted it up himself.
sentences.zh: 他自己把它涂上了颜色。

sentences.en: And I showed him how to attach the wheels on and he did that.
sentences.zh: 我教他怎么装上轮子，他照做了。

sentences.en: So I played a role kind of showing him how to do things.
sentences.zh: 所以我扮演了一个展示他如何做事的角色。

sentences.en: But then when we showed up, all the other cars were beautifully crasped.
sentences.zh: 但当我们到场时，所有其他的车都工艺精美。

sentences.en: They were just so smooth, perfectly painted.
sentences.zh: 它们是如此光滑，完美涂漆。

sentences.en: And my son and I, we just almost left.
sentences.zh: 我和我儿子，我们差点就离开了。

sentences.en: We didn't even want...
sentences.zh: 我们甚至不想……

sentences.en: His looked like it was made by an eight-year-old, right?
sentences.zh: 他的看起来像是八岁小孩做的，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I'm assuming the car probably didn't run as smoothly as some of the other cars that
sentences.zh: 我猜这辆车的运行可能不像其他车那么平稳，

sentences.en: had the superior craftsmanship of it.
sentences.zh: 那些车拥有更精湛的工艺。

sentences.en: It did not run as smoothly as the others.
sentences.zh: 它的确没有其他车运行得那么平稳。

sentences.en: And I think the others refrained from laughing at us, but we were embarrassed.
sentences.zh: 我想其他人克制住了没有嘲笑我们，但我们很尴尬。

sentences.en: So there's a common pattern to all of these stories, Peter.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些故事都有一个共同的模式，彼得。

sentences.en: A number of years ago, you began taking notice of what adults are doing when they interact
sentences.zh: 几年前，你开始注意到成年人在与

sentences.en: with kids.
sentences.zh: 孩子互动时在做什么。

sentences.en: What did you notice?
sentences.zh: 你注意到了什么？

sentences.en: In many ways, adults have taken over children's lives.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，成年人已经接管了孩子的生活。

sentences.en: I think in some sense with good intentions.
sentences.zh: 我认为从某种意义上说，这是出于好意。

sentences.en: There's a lot of promotion of the idea that parents should be very much involved with their
sentences.zh: 有一种观点得到了广泛宣传，即父母应该极大地参与到他们

sentences.en: children's lives, that parents are expected almost these days, much more so than in the
sentences.zh: 孩子的生活中，如今人们几乎期望父母这样做，比

sentences.en: past, to kind of be teachers to their children, as well as comforters and nurturers and so on.
sentences.zh: 过去要多得多，有点像孩子的老师，以及安慰者和培育者等等。

sentences.en: And I think the cost of that has been that it takes away from children's own initiative,
sentences.zh: 我认为这样做的代价是，它剥夺了儿童自己的主动性，

sentences.en: from children's own opportunities to figure things out for themselves.
sentences.zh: 剥夺了儿童自己弄清楚事情的机会。

sentences.en: And learn how to solve probleMs.
sentences.zh: 并学会如何解决问题。

sentences.en: You write that children perceive adults as potential enforcers of safety, solvers of
sentences.zh: 你写道，儿童将成年人视为安全的潜在执行者、

sentences.en: conflicts, and audiences for whining.
sentences.zh: 冲突的解决者，以及抱怨的听众。

sentences.en: And this perception invites the children to act unsafely, to squabble, and to whine.
sentences.zh: 这种看法促使儿童表现得不安全、争吵和抱怨。

sentences.en: Expand on that.
sentences.zh: 请展开谈谈。

sentences.en: Tell me what you mean.
sentences.zh: 告诉我你是什么意思。

sentences.en: In my experience, children actually take responsibility when there's no adults around.
sentences.zh: 以我的经验，当周围没有成年人时，孩子们实际上会承担责任。

sentences.en: That's part of the advantage of there being no adults around.
sentences.zh: 这就是周围没有成年人的好处之一。

sentences.en: They have to take responsibility.
sentences.zh: 他们必须承担责任。

sentences.en: If there's no adults there to tell you what to do, you've got to kind of say, well, is
sentences.zh: 如果没有大人在那里告诉你该做什么，你大概会说，嗯，这是

sentences.en: this safe or not safe?
sentences.zh: 安全还是不安全？

sentences.en: Is this a reasonable thing to do or not?
sentences.zh: 这是一件合理的事情还是不合理？

sentences.en: And children are pretty good at that.
sentences.zh: 孩子们在这方面相当擅长。

sentences.en: But when there's adults around, at least in this day and age, they kind of assume the
sentences.zh: 但当有成年人在场时，至少在这个时代，他们会认为

sentences.en: adults are responsible for deciding if it's safe or not.
sentences.zh: 成年人有责任决定是否安全。

sentences.en: The adults are responsible.
sentences.zh: 成年人负有责任。

sentences.en: If somebody's teasing you instead of for you to figure out, what am I going to do about
sentences.zh: 如果有人在取笑你，而不是让你去想，我要怎么处理

sentences.en: this person who's teasing me?
sentences.zh: 这个取笑我的人？

sentences.en: You go and tell the adult.
sentences.zh: 你去告诉成年人。

sentences.en: So even just the mere presence of adults influences the way children play.
sentences.zh: 所以，仅仅是成年人的存在就会影响儿童玩耍的方式。

sentences.en: When kids are left to themselves, they don't automatically become rule breakers.
sentences.zh: 当把孩子们留给他们自己时，他们不会自动成为破坏规则的人。

sentences.en: That's the way it may seem from a grown-up perspective.
sentences.zh: 从成年人的视角来看，情况可能确实如此。

sentences.en: But really, Peter says, when kids play by themselves, they learn to become rule inventors.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，彼得说，当孩子们自己玩耍时，他们学会成为规则的创造者。

sentences.en: Peter learned this at a family gathering when a couple of 10-year-old girls invited him
sentences.zh: 彼得在一次家庭聚会上了解到这一点，当时几个10岁的女孩邀请他

sentences.en: to join their game of Scrabble.
sentences.zh: 加入她们的拼字游戏。

sentences.en: So I kind of assumed, well, this is an opportunity for me to sort of teach them about Scrabble.
sentences.zh: 所以我有点以为，嗯，这是一个我向她们传授拼字游戏的机会。

sentences.en: I'm pretty good at Scrabble, and I'm sure they're novices.
sentences.zh: 我擅长拼字游戏，而她们肯定还是新手。

sentences.en: And I sat down to play Scrabble with them and started to explain the rules.
sentences.zh: 我坐下来和她们玩拼字游戏，开始解释规则。

sentences.en: But they had played the game before and went right into a game that was modeled after Scrabble,
sentences.zh: 但她们以前玩过这个游戏，直接进入了一个以拼字游戏为蓝本的游戏，

sentences.en: but it had their own rules.
sentences.zh: 但它有她们自己的规则。

sentences.en: So instead of having to play an actual word, they could play any kind of a nonsense word
sentences.zh: 因此，她们不必拼出一个真正的单词，而是可以拼出任何胡言乱语的单词

sentences.en: as long as it sounded like a word.
sentences.zh: 只要听起来像个词就行。

sentences.en: And the longer and sillier it sounded, the better.
sentences.zh: 而且听起来越长、越荒谬越好。

sentences.en: They had no interest in keeping score.
sentences.zh: 他们对记分毫无兴趣。

sentences.en: You know, they were just having a great time playing nonsense words.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们只是在开心地玩胡言乱语的游戏。

sentences.en: And then they would once in a while challenge the other person, what's the meaning of this?
sentences.zh: 然后他们偶尔会挑战对方，这到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: And then the other one would pretend to look it up in the dictionary and cite a very funny meaning
sentences.zh: 接着另一个人会假装在字典里查阅，并引述一个非常搞笑的意思

sentences.en: that fit a little bit with the way it sounded.
sentences.zh: 这个意思多多少少和它的发音有点契合。

sentences.en: And I just sat back after a little bit of protesting.
sentences.zh: 稍微抗议了一会儿后，我就靠回了椅背上。

sentences.en: Hey, this is Scrabble.
sentences.zh: 嘿，这是拼字游戏。

sentences.en: Let's really play Scrabble.
sentences.zh: 我们来真正地玩一局拼字游戏吧。

sentences.en: I just finally sat back and I realized, hey, these girls are really playing.
sentences.zh: 我最后终于靠回椅背上意识到，嘿，这些女孩是来真格的。

sentences.en: My way of playing Scrabble is a little bit more like work than like play.
sentences.zh: 我玩拼字游戏的方式与其说是玩，不如说更像是在工作。

sentences.en: I understand your son, Scott, gave you something of a window into the effects that adults can have on children.
sentences.zh: 我了解到，你的儿子斯科特让你对成年人可能对孩子产生的影响有了一些直观的了解。

sentences.en: He was not a fan of elementary school, and perhaps that's putting it mildly.
sentences.zh: 他可不是小学的粉丝，也许这种说法还算委婉的。

sentences.en: Putting it mildly is correct.
sentences.zh: 说委婉点确实没错。

sentences.en: He hated school right from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 他从一开始就讨厌学校。

sentences.en: And he complained all the way from kindergarten through fourth grade.
sentences.zh: 从幼儿园到四年级，他一路都在抱怨。

sentences.en: He would come home and be angry.
sentences.zh: 他回到家总是很生气。

sentences.en: He would say, you know, they're acting like I'm a puppet and I'm supposed to just do what they're telling me to do,
sentences.zh: 他会说，你知道的，他们把我当成提线木偶，让我必须按照他们说的去做，

sentences.en: and I have no say in it.
sentences.zh: 而我一点发言权也没有。

sentences.en: And, of course, that's the way school works.
sentences.zh: 当然，学校就是这样运作的。

sentences.en: And I would say to him, well, just do what they tell you to do.
sentences.zh: 我会对他说，听着，照他们说的做就行了。

sentences.en: You know, it's not that hard.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这没那么难。

sentences.en: Just do it.
sentences.zh: 照做就是了。

sentences.en: You know, all kids in some ways have conflicts with parents and teachers.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所有孩子在某种程度上都会与父母和老师产生冲突。

sentences.en: And so, you know, kids are unhappy at school.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，孩子们在学校里并不开心。

sentences.en: They're distracted.
sentences.zh: 他们总是分心。

sentences.en: They're bored.
sentences.zh: 他们感到无聊。

sentences.en: They talk to their friends instead of studying or paying attention in class.
sentences.zh: 他们在课堂上跟朋友聊天，而不是学习或专心听讲。

sentences.en: And, you know, they run into their run-ins with teachers.
sentences.zh: 而且，你懂的，他们跟老师之间总免不了产生摩擦。

sentences.en: I mean, this is a routine part of childhood for almost all kids.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这对几乎所有孩子来说都是童年的常规部分。

sentences.en: What was he doing that was different?
sentences.zh: 他做的事情有什么不同呢？

sentences.en: Was it actually, was it just that garden variety kind of rebellion, or was it something more than that?
sentences.zh: 这实际上只是那种司空见惯的叛逆，还是有更深层次的原因？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, his rebellion was very different from the typical, you know, naughty boy, you know, who's maybe shooting spitballs and so on.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，他的叛逆与典型的、你知道的淘气男孩非常不同，那种可能会吐纸团之类的男孩。

sentences.en: His rebellion was almost like a planned rebellion.
sentences.zh: 他的叛逆几乎像是有计划的叛逆。

sentences.en: It was – so just for example, when the teacher would teach him a specific way of doing arithmetic problems and how you're supposed to show your work,
sentences.zh: 那就是——举个例子，当老师教给他做算术题的特定方法以及如何写出解题步骤时，

sentences.en: he would deliberately find a different way to do it.
sentences.zh: 他会故意找一种不同的方法来做。

sentences.en: And then the teachers complained to us about that, and I asked him, so why do you do it a different way?
sentences.zh: 然后老师向我们抱怨这件事，我问他，你为什么偏要用不同的方法呢？

sentences.en: And he said, it's because it's the only way I can make it fun.
sentences.zh: 他说，因为这是我能把它变得有趣的唯一方法。

sentences.en: And when they were teaching about punctuation and capital letters and how to put them into sentences,
sentences.zh: 当他们学习标点符号、大写字母以及如何把它们放入句子中时，

sentences.en: he actually declared, I'm going to write now like A.E.
sentences.zh: 他居然宣称，我现在要像诗人E.E.

sentences.en: Cummings, the poet, and put punctuation and capitals wherever I please.
sentences.zh: 卡明斯那样写作，想把标点符号和大写字母加在哪里就加在哪里。

sentences.en: So that was him.
sentences.zh: 这就是他。

sentences.en: Ultimately, it led to a meeting in the principal's office in which his teacher, the principal, assistant principal, school psychologist,
sentences.zh: 最终，这导致了一场校长办公室的会议，他的老师、校长、副校长、学校心理学家、

sentences.en: another psychologist called from outside, his mom and me were all there to tell him in no uncertain terms
sentences.zh: 另一位从外面请来的心理学家、他的妈妈和我都在场，毫不含糊地告诉他

sentences.en: that he had to follow the rules of the school.
sentences.zh: 他必须遵守学校的规章制度。

sentences.en: And he, nine years old, looked at us big adults and he said, go to hell.
sentences.zh: 而他，一个九岁的孩子，看着我们这一群大人说，见鬼去吧。

sentences.en: As a dad, Peter knew something had to change.
sentences.zh: 作为父亲，彼得知道必须做出改变了。

sentences.en: But as a researcher, he started to ask himself, is it possible the problem was not with kids like Scott, but with adults like himself?
sentences.zh: 但作为一名研究人员，他开始问自己，有没有可能问题不在于像斯科特这样的孩子，而在于像他这样的成年人？

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是《隐形大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹坦。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐形大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹坦。

sentences.en: When it comes to rearing happy and healthy children, when should we lend a helping hand?
sentences.zh: 在抚养快乐健康的儿童方面，我们什么时候该伸出援手？

sentences.en: And when should we step away and let kids figure out things for themselves?
sentences.zh: 又什么时候该退一步，让孩子们自己去摸索？

sentences.en: At Boston College, psychologist Peter Gray studies what adults today do and what they ought to do to maximize the well-being of children.
sentences.zh: 在波士顿学院，心理学家彼得·格雷专门研究如今的成年人做了什么，以及他们为了让儿童福祉最大化应该做些什么。

sentences.en: He says an important question parents, teachers, and school administrators should ask themselves when it comes to rules and structure is how much is too much?
sentences.zh: 他说，当涉及到规则和结构时，父母、老师和学校管理者应该问自己一个重要问题：究竟多少才算太多？

sentences.en: Peter, you decided to start your research by delving into what anthropologists have found about child-rearing practices throughout human history.
sentences.zh: 彼得，你决定通过深入了解人类历史上人类学家发现的育儿做法来开始你的研究。

sentences.en: What was the typical pattern before modern times?
sentences.zh: 在现代之前，典型的模式是什么样的？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I began to get interested in how children historically have acquired the culture that they're growing up in,
sentences.zh: 所以我开始对儿童在历史上是如何习得他们成长的文化的产生兴趣，

sentences.en: learning from others what you need to know to succeed in that culture eventually as an adult.
sentences.zh: 向他人学习在未来作为成年人该文化中生存所需要知道的知识。

sentences.en: And I'm an evolutionary psychologist, so I look at human nature from the perspective of Darwinian evolution.
sentences.zh: 我是一名进化心理学家，所以我从达尔文进化的角度来看待人性。

sentences.en: If you look at human nature from that perspective, you automatically become interested in hunter-gatherers
sentences.zh: 如果你从这个角度来看待人性，你自然就会对狩猎采集者感兴趣，

sentences.en: because we were all hunter-gatherers during 99% or so of our biological evolution.
sentences.zh: 因为在我们生物进化的99%左右的时间里，我们全都是狩猎采集者。

sentences.en: And as you undoubtedly know, there have been hunter-gatherers in isolated parts of the world who, at least into the middle to even late 20th century,
sentences.zh: 正如你毫无疑问所知，世界上一些偏远地区仍然存在着狩猎采集者，至少在20世纪中叶甚至晚期，

sentences.en: were still living in a rather pristine hunter-gatherer way of life.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然过着相当原始的狩猎采集生活方式。

sentences.en: And there were anthropologists who had trekked out into those areas to make contact with them and study them.
sentences.zh: 当时有人类学家跋涉到那些地区去接触他们并研究他们。

sentences.en: And I began to read what I could of such work and ultimately, along with a graduate student,
sentences.zh: 我开始阅读我能找到的此类工作，最终，和一名研究生一起，

sentences.en: surveyed a group of anthropologists who had studied various different groups of hunter-gatherers in different parts of the world
sentences.zh: 调查了一组曾研究过世界不同地区各种不同狩猎采集群体的人类学家，

sentences.en: to find out from them what are children's lives like in the culture that they observe?
sentences.zh: 从他们那里了解在他们所观察的文化中孩子的生活是怎样的？

sentences.en: What's the relationship between adults and children?
sentences.zh: 成年人与儿童之间的关系是怎样的？

sentences.en: And what I found, in every case, seven different cultures on three different continents,
sentences.zh: 我发现，在每一种情况下——横跨三个不同大陆的七种不同文化中，

sentences.en: was that the children were free to play and explore pretty much all day long.
sentences.zh: 孩子们基本上整天都可以自由地玩耍和探索。

sentences.en: They might be asked to do little chores, but no such thing as school.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会被要求做点小零活，但根本没有什么学校这种东西。

sentences.en: You know, the adults might say, you know, don't eat these mushrooms, they're poisonous.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，成年人可能会说，别吃这些蘑菇，它们有毒。

sentences.en: They would point out things that are dangerous.
sentences.zh: 他们会指出危险的事物。

sentences.en: But the assumption was that children would learn by observing, by exploring, by playing.
sentences.zh: 但默认的假设是，孩子们会通过观察、探索和玩耍来学习。

sentences.en: And when I asked the anthropologists, well, what did the children play at?
sentences.zh: 当我问人类学家，孩子们都在玩些什么呢？

sentences.en: They talked about play that seemed to be, in essentially every case,
sentences.zh: 他们谈到的游戏在基本上每一种情况下似乎都

sentences.en: modeled after the activities that were important to the culture in which they were growing up.
sentences.zh: 以他们成长过程中对该文化重要的活动为模版。

sentences.en: So, in a culture where the men hunt big game, the little boys and middle-sized boys, too, were playing at hunting big game.
sentences.zh: 所以，在一个男人们猎捕大型猎物的文化中，小男孩和大一点的男孩们也在玩猎捕大型猎物的游戏。

sentences.en: In a culture where they used dugout canoes, the kids were playing with dugout canoes, and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 在一个使用独木舟的文化中，孩子们就在玩独木舟的游戏，诸如此类。

sentences.en: They played at the games and music and art of the culture.
sentences.zh: 他们玩该文化的各种游戏、音乐和艺术。

sentences.en: And not because anybody was requiring them to do so, but because it just seemed apparently natural for them to do that.
sentences.zh: 这并不是因为有人要求他们这么做，而是因为这样做对他们来说似乎是顺理成章、自然而然的。

sentences.en: And what the anthropologists pointed out is they would play at these things, and eventually they were actually doing these things.
sentences.zh: 人类学家指出的是，他们通过玩这些东西，最终他们实际上就在做这些事情了。

sentences.en: The play would merge into adult-like activities.
sentences.zh: 玩耍会融合成类似成年的活动。

sentences.en: So, there was no real difference between what you're doing when you're playing
sentences.zh: 因此，你在玩耍时所做的事情，

sentences.en: and what you're doing when you're an adult actually doing this thing that you were playing at before.
sentences.zh: 和你作为成年人真正去做你之前一直在扮演的这种事情之间，并没有真正的区别。

sentences.en: So, this was very interesting to me.
sentences.zh: 所以，这让我非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: And, of course, the children would have been hanging out with a range of other children, probably of different ages.
sentences.zh: 当然，孩子们会和各种各样的其他孩子混在一起，可能年龄各不相同。

sentences.en: Presumably, they would be learning not just from children who are exactly their own age,
sentences.zh: 据推测，他们不仅会向年龄完全相同的孩子学习，

sentences.en: but from children who are a little older.
sentences.zh: 还会向稍微大一点的孩子学习。

sentences.en: And those children might have learned things from children who are a little older than them.
sentences.zh: 而那些孩子可能已经从比他们稍大一点的孩子那里学到了东西。

sentences.en: That's a very important observation, that these are all band cultures.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常重要的观察结果，即这些都是游群文化。

sentences.en: So, they're relatively small.
sentences.zh: 所以它们的规模相对较小。

sentences.en: Even if you wanted to just hang out with kids your own age, there wouldn't be enough.
sentences.zh: 即使你只想和同龄的孩子厮混在一起，人数也不够。

sentences.en: So, you're always playing with kids who are both older and younger than yourself.
sentences.zh: 所以你总是在和比你大或比你小的孩子一起玩。

sentences.en: So, a typical play group might be kids from age 4 to 12 or age 8 to 16, all playing together.
sentences.zh: 因此，典型的游戏群体可能是4到12岁或8到16岁的孩子，大家一起玩。

sentences.en: But when children are playing across age, the younger children are always learning from the older children.
sentences.zh: 但当孩子们跨年龄玩耍时，较小的孩子总是在向较大的孩子学习。

sentences.en: They're being boosted up to higher levels of activity.
sentences.zh: 他们被提升到了更高的活动水平。

sentences.en: And the older children are, in very important ways, learning from younger children.
sentences.zh: 而较大的孩子在非常重要的方面也在向较小的孩子学习。

sentences.en: They're learning how to be leaders.
sentences.zh: 他们在学习如何成为领导者。

sentences.en: They're learning how to be caretakers.
sentences.zh: 他们在学习如何成为照顾者。

sentences.en: They're learning, in some sense, how to be teachers as they're explaining to the younger children how to do whatever it is that they're doing.
sentences.zh: 当他们向较小的孩子解释如何做他们正在做的事情时，他们在某种意义上学习了如何成为老师。

sentences.en: So, your research suggests that when adults leave children alone to play and learn and socialize in their own way, kids become more likely to develop a range of skills.
sentences.zh: 所以，你的研究表明，当成年人让孩子们独自玩耍、学习并以他们自己的方式进行社交时，孩子们更有可能培养出一系列技能。

sentences.en: Like what, Peter?
sentences.zh: 比如什么，彼得？

sentences.en: I could really run through all of the basic skills that children have to develop in any culture in order to succeed.
sentences.zh: 我其实可以把孩子们为了在任何文化中取得成功而必须培养的所有基本技能过一遍。

sentences.en: These are social skills.
sentences.zh: 这些就是社交技能。

sentences.en: These are the skills of knowing how to initiate an activity and direct that activity, problem-solving skills.
sentences.zh: 这些是知道如何发起一项活动并指导该活动的技能，以及解决问题的技能。

sentences.en: Children practice these skills when they're playing and when they're playing with other children.
sentences.zh: 孩子们在玩耍以及和其他孩子一起玩耍时会练习这些技能。

sentences.en: When adults are around, adults step in and solve the problems for the children.
sentences.zh: 当成年人在场时，成年人会介入并为孩子们解决问题。

sentences.en: The adults tell them how to play and that children, therefore, are not learning how to take initiative, not learning how to create rules for themselves,
sentences.zh: 成年人会告诉他们如何玩耍，因此孩子们就没有学会如何采取主动，没有学会如何为自己制定规则，

sentences.en: not learning how to negotiate with other children to solve probleMs.
sentences.zh: 没有学会如何与其他孩子协商来解决问题。

sentences.en: If there's always an adult there, doing it for them.
sentences.zh: 如果总有一个成年人在那里代劳的话。

sentences.en: And in some ways, I suppose all of this points back to the central thing that children need to learn, which is to learn to be independent.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，我想这一切都指向了孩子们需要学习的核心内容，那就是学会独立。

sentences.en: Perhaps we're taking that away from them.
sentences.zh: 也许我们正在剥夺他们的这一点。

sentences.en: That's well put.
sentences.zh: 说得好。

sentences.en: Because, again, from an evolutionary perspective, when do we even have this long period of childhood?
sentences.zh: 因为再次从进化的角度来看，我们为什么会拥有如此漫长的童年期？

sentences.en: What is the purpose of the juvenile period, as we would say, in all mammals?
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，所有哺乳动物中幼年期的目的是什么？

sentences.en: It is to develop the skills that allow you to become increasingly independent.
sentences.zh: 它是为了培养能让你变得越来越独立的技能。

sentences.en: But the only way you can develop those skills is by being allowed increasing amounts of independence as you are growing older from year to year.
sentences.zh: 但你培养这些技能的唯一途径，就是在随着年龄一年年增长的过程中，被允许获得越来越多的独立性。

sentences.en: That used to occur in our culture.
sentences.zh: 这过去在我们的文化中是存在的。

sentences.en: That was certainly true when I was a child many, many decades ago.
sentences.zh: 几十年前我还是个孩子的时候确实如此。

sentences.en: And it was even true when my son was a child fewer decades ago.
sentences.zh: 甚至在几十年后的我儿子小时候也是如此。

sentences.en: But today, we are not allowing children to do the things that they should be doing, that they're capable of doing, for a variety of reasons.
sentences.zh: 但今天，由于各种原因，我们不再允许孩子们去做他们应该做的事情，去做他们有能力做的事情。

sentences.en: But the end result is that children are more or less supervised, directed, monitored, corrected all the time.
sentences.zh: 但最终的结果是，孩子们或多或少一直在被监督、指导、监控和纠正。

sentences.en: You say that when children spend a lot of time in the company of adults, they're less likely to participate in what you call authentic communication.
sentences.zh: 你说，当孩子们花大量时间与成年人在一起时，他们参与你所谓的真实交流的可能性就会降低。

sentences.en: And they're more likely to do this when they're in the company of other children.
sentences.zh: 而当他们与其他孩子在一起时，他们更有可能这样做。

sentences.en: What do you mean by this term, Peter?
sentences.zh: 彼得，你这个术语是什么意思？

sentences.en: Let me refer to a research study that was done some time ago.
sentences.zh: 让我参考一下不久前做的一项研究。

sentences.en: These researchers recorded children's voices while they were playing with other children.
sentences.zh: 这些研究人员记录了孩子们与其他孩子玩耍时的声音。

sentences.en: These were young children, about probably five or six years old.
sentences.zh: 这些是年幼的孩子，大概五六岁左右。

sentences.en: And then also recorded them when they were in class talking with their teacher.
sentences.zh: 然后还记录了他们在课堂上与老师交谈时的声音。

sentences.en: And also recorded them when they were just sitting around having lunch.
sentences.zh: 还记录了他们只是坐在一起吃午饭时的声音。

sentences.en: When they were playing, the language was far more sophisticated, far more real, far more authentic than in any other situation.
sentences.zh: 当他们玩耍时，语言要复杂得多、真实得多、地道得多，超过了任何其他情况。

sentences.en: Because when you're playing with other kids, you're constantly negotiating.
sentences.zh: 因为当你和别的孩子玩耍时，你一直在协商。

sentences.en: You know, maybe picture a group of young children playing that they're going to the king's ball.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，也许可以想象一群小孩子在玩假装去参加国王舞会的游戏。

sentences.en: And, you know, who's going to marry the prince?
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，谁来嫁给王子？

sentences.en: And so then there's a discussion about that.
sentences.zh: 于是就有了关于这个的讨论。

sentences.en: Or who gets to wear this beautiful set of necklaces that you find in the dress-up corner of the kindergarten room.
sentences.zh: 或者谁能戴上你在幼儿园换装角落里找到的这套漂亮项链。

sentences.en: And so there's constant.
sentences.zh: 所以一直都在。

sentences.en: They spend more time negotiating and discussing what they're doing than actually playing it out.
sentences.zh: 他们花在协商和讨论他们正在做的事情上的时间，比实际把它们演出来的时间还要多。

sentences.en: Which is a good thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一件好事。

sentences.en: Because that's how you think of what they're learning when they do that.
sentences.zh: 因为这就是你如何看待他们在这样做时所学到的东西。

sentences.en: They're learning this incredibly important skill of being able to use words, language, to decide mutually what they're doing as a group.
sentences.zh: 他们正在学习这种极其重要的技能，即能够使用言语和语言来共同决定他们作为一个群体正在做什么。

sentences.en: How are we going to play this game?
sentences.zh: 我们该怎么玩这个游戏？

sentences.en: You say that when kids interact with adults, they don't get the same kind of authentic feedback that they get when they are interacting with other children.
sentences.zh: 你曾说，当孩子们与成年人互动时，他们无法获得与他们和其他孩子互动时那种同等程度的真实反馈。

sentences.en: Can you give me some examples of what you mean by this?
sentences.zh: 你能举几个例子说明你的意思吗？

sentences.en: Well, you know, sometimes it's just ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，有时这简直太荒谬了。

sentences.en: You'll hear a parent or an adult say to a child, so, Billy, what color is that?
sentences.zh: 你经常会听到父母或成年人对孩子说：嗨，比利，那是什么颜色？

sentences.en: Oh, my gosh.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: This is so patronizing.
sentences.zh: 这太居高临下了。

sentences.en: You know, it's as if the purpose of the discussion is always kind of pedantic to try to teach the child something rather than an actual authentic back-and-forth discussion.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就好像对话的目的总是带有某种学究气，试图教给孩子点什么，而不是进行真正地、地地道道的来回交流。

sentences.en: And I suppose also there is some pressure that parents and teachers feel to give positive feedback.
sentences.zh: 而且我想，父母和老师也会感受到提供积极反馈的一些压力。

sentences.en: So, when, you know, the four-year-old comes back with a scribble on a page, there is some pressure to say this is a masterpiece.
sentences.zh: 所以，当四岁的孩子拿着一张涂鸦跑过来时，就会有一种压力，非得说这是一件杰作不可。

sentences.en: Yes, unlike kids.
sentences.zh: 是的，跟小孩子们不一样。

sentences.en: You know, I'll give you what I think is a nice example of this.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我给你讲一个我认为很好的例子。

sentences.en: So, in one of the situations where I was observing age mixed play and how seven- and eight-year-old children playing card games with children who are somewhat older,
sentences.zh: 当时我正在观察混合年龄的游戏，以及七八岁的孩子是如何和稍大一些的孩子一起玩纸牌游戏的，

sentences.en: and I was observing how the older children would keep the younger children on task.
sentences.zh: 我观察到大一点的孩子是如何让小一点的孩子专注于任务的。

sentences.en: And they would say things like, hey, stupid, you know, pay attention.
sentences.zh: 他们会说这样的话：嘿，笨蛋，注意听着。

sentences.en: You know, this is not what a typical parent today would say.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这可不是现在典型的父母会说的话。

sentences.en: But the kids, I think, actually, the little kids, I think, appreciated that because this is genuine coming from an older kid.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，小孩子们其实很感激这一点，因为这是大孩子发自内心的真性情。

sentences.en: This kid is not trying to patronize you in some way.
sentences.zh: 这个孩子并不是在变着法儿地居高临下地对你。

sentences.en: You also say that in the course of playing, children come to understand that rules, in fact, are invented things.
sentences.zh: 你还提到，在玩耍的过程中，孩子们逐渐理解到规则其实是人发明出来的。

sentences.en: They are things that have been invented by other people and that they can be modified and changed.
sentences.zh: 它们是其他人发明的东西，是可以被修改和改变的。

sentences.en: And it's harder to do that if you believe that rules are sacrosanct and handed down to you by an all-powerful adult.
sentences.zh: 如果你认为规则是神圣不可侵犯的，是由一个全能的成年人传授给你的，那么你就很难做到这一点。

sentences.en: One way to think about this is the difference between, let's say, Little League Baseball, a pickup game of baseball, the way we used to play it when I was a kid.
sentences.zh: 思考这个问题的一个方法是，比方说，比较一下少儿棒球联盟和那种随性自发的棒球野球局，也就是我小时候那种玩法。

sentences.en: You know, there would be a bunch of kids who would show up in the vacant lot and there was never 18 players.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，会有一群孩子出现在空地上，但从来凑不够18个人。

sentences.en: We had to kind of figure out how we're going to make up the sides.
sentences.zh: 我们得自己想办法怎么分队。

sentences.en: We had to create ground rules.
sentences.zh: 我们必须制定基本规则。

sentences.en: Anything, you know, hit in the direction of those windows over there, that's an automatic out and so on.
sentences.zh: 比如，任何打向那边那些窗户方向的球，都算直接出局，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Have to pitch soft to little Timmy.
sentences.zh: 给小蒂米投球时动作得柔和点。

sentences.en: We'd make up all the rules so there'd be fun for everybody and fair for everybody.
sentences.zh: 我们会制定所有的规则，好让每个人都玩得开心，对每个人都公平。

sentences.en: This is just the way kids always play.
sentences.zh: 这正是孩子们一贯的玩法。

sentences.en: Little League, you play by the official rules of baseball.
sentences.zh: 而在少儿棒球联盟里，你得按照棒球的官方规则来打。

sentences.en: You don't vary them.
sentences.zh: 你不能改变它们。

sentences.en: You just do it.
sentences.zh: 你照做就行了。

sentences.en: And there's adults there making sure you follow those rules.
sentences.zh: 而且现场有成年人盯着，确保你遵守这些规则。

sentences.en: You say that one reason adults are less inclined to give children the freedom they used to have is that adults are increasingly concerned about their children's safety.
sentences.zh: 你说，成年人越来越不愿意给孩子过去那种自由的原因之一，是成年人越来越担心孩子的安全。

sentences.en: When did this fear arise, Peter?
sentences.zh: 彼得，这种恐惧是什么时候出现的？

sentences.en: And how does it affect the lives of children?
sentences.zh: 它又是如何影响儿童生活的？

sentences.en: So when I was a kid many decades ago, the regular song of parents was, get out of the house.
sentences.zh: 所以，几十年前我还是个孩子的时候，父母的常态口头禅就是：滚出去。

sentences.en: Get out of the house.
sentences.zh: 滚出去。

sentences.en: I don't want you around.
sentences.zh: 我不想看见你在周围晃悠。

sentences.en: So kids were outdoors and they'd find one another and they'd play with one another.
sentences.zh: 所以孩子们都在户外，他们会找到彼此，一起玩耍。

sentences.en: This was not just the 1950s and 1960s America.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是二十世纪五十和六十年代的美国。

sentences.en: This is the way hunter-gatherer children played, as I described before.
sentences.zh: 正如我之前所描述的那样，这就是采集狩猎社会的孩子们的玩耍方式。

sentences.en: This is generally the way children throughout the world have played.
sentences.zh: 这也是全世界儿童普遍的玩耍方式。

sentences.en: And so this is a new thing, in some sense, in the history of the world, where we are not allowing children independent activity away from adults.
sentences.zh: 因此，从某种意义上说，这是世界历史上的一种新现象，我们不再允许儿童在没有成年人陪伴的情况下进行独立的活动。

sentences.en: We've got adults around them all the time.
sentences.zh: 我们时时刻刻都有成年人在他们身边。

sentences.en: But talk a little bit about sort of the concern for safety and sort of the concern that many parents have,
sentences.zh: 但请谈谈关于安全的担忧，以及许多父母所担心的一种情况，

sentences.en: that if they were to give kids the kind of freedom that they had before, that bad things could happen to them.
sentences.zh: 那就是如果他们给孩子以前那种自由，不好的事情可能会降临到他们头上。

sentences.en: Yeah, so if you ask parents why they're not allowing their children outside, you'll get a variety of answers.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以如果你问父母为什么不让孩子去户外，你会得到各种各样的回答。

sentences.en: Some of them are quite legitimate.
sentences.zh: 其中一些是相当合理的。

sentences.en: One of them is, well, there's nobody else outside.
sentences.zh: 其中一个原因是，外面根本没有别人。

sentences.en: And so my child goes outside to play and there's nobody to play with.
sentences.zh: 所以我的孩子去外面玩，却找不到人一起玩。

sentences.en: Or, you know, I've heard of this case recently in our neighborhood where somebody let their child out to play with other children.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道，我最近在我们社区听说过这样一件事：有人让他们的孩子出去和别的孩子玩。

sentences.en: And somebody called the police and then protective services arrived.
sentences.zh: 结果有人报警了，接着儿童保护服务机构就赶到了。

sentences.en: So the culture has changed such that you are considered to be a negligent parent if you allow your child outside without observing that child.
sentences.zh: 因此，文化已经发生了变化，如果你允许孩子在不被看管的情况下外出，你就会被认为是不负责任的父母。

sentences.en: Now, why did the culture change?
sentences.zh: 那么，文化为什么会改变呢？

sentences.en: And I think that the biggest change occurred in the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 我认为最大的变化发生在二十世纪八十年代。

sentences.en: There were a couple of cases of young boys.
sentences.zh: 当时有几个关于小男孩的案例。

sentences.en: In both cases, they were six years old.
sentences.zh: 在这两个案例中，他们都只有六岁。

sentences.en: One of these instances occurred actually in 1979 and the other in 1981, who were taken by a stranger on the street and ultimately murdered.
sentences.zh: 其中一起事件实际上发生在1979年，另一起发生在1981年，他们在街上被陌生人带走，并最终遭到杀害。

sentences.en: This is, of course, a very rare event.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是一件非常罕见的事情。

sentences.en: And because it's rare, it made headlines.
sentences.zh: 正因为罕见，它成了头条新闻。

sentences.en: It was in the news all the time.
sentences.zh: 它一直出现在新闻里。

sentences.en: And it led to programs trying to protect, make sure that this doesn't happen again.
sentences.zh: 这促使人们推出各种项目，试图进行保护，以确保这种事情不再发生。

sentences.en: And among those programs was to put pictures on milk cartons of missing children.
sentences.zh: 在这些项目当中，就包括把失踪儿童的照片印在牛奶盒上。

sentences.en: And the assumption was that when you were eating your breakfast cereal and looking at this milk carton, that these missing children were people,
sentences.zh: 人们当时的假设是，当你吃着早餐麦片看着这个牛奶盒时，这些失踪儿童就是那些人，

sentences.en: little kids who had been snatched away by some stranger on the street.
sentences.zh: 是被街上的某个陌生人拐走的小孩。

sentences.en: And the whole concept of stranger danger was developed.
sentences.zh: 整个“防范陌生人”的概念就是这样发展起来的。

sentences.en: And once a person has this image in their head, it's hard to get it out of your head.
sentences.zh: 一旦一个人脑子里有了这种印象，就很难把它赶出脑海。

sentences.en: So it leads to a belief that the world is more dangerous than it actually is.
sentences.zh: 这导致了一种信念，即世界比实际情况更加危险。

sentences.en: The truth of the matter is the world is not more dangerous today than it was decades ago.
sentences.zh: 事实的真相是，今天的世界并不比几十年前更危险。

sentences.en: You know, it's also the case that families are having fewer children today.
sentences.zh: 你知道，现在的家庭生孩子也越来越少了。

sentences.en: This is not just in the United States.
sentences.zh: 这不仅在美国是这样。

sentences.en: It's in many countries around the world.
sentences.zh: 世界上许多国家都是如此。

sentences.en: And I'm not necessarily suggesting that parents who have many kids, you know, love their children any less than parents who have few kids.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说生很多孩子的父母，你知道的，爱他们的孩子就会比生少数孩子的父母少。

sentences.en: But it is certainly the case that I think parents direct more attention to their kids now, in part because families are smaller.
sentences.zh: 但可以肯定的是，我认为父母现在对孩子的关注更多了，部分原因是因为家庭规模变小了。

sentences.en: And that's driven by, you know, demographic and economic changes that are probably well beyond the control of any individual.
sentences.zh: 这是由人口和经济变化驱动的，这些变化可能远远超出了任何个人的控制范围。

sentences.en: I think that is definitely a contributing factor.
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝对是一个促成因素。

sentences.en: When you have more kids, you're more likely to want some of them out of the house, if not all of them out of the house, right?
sentences.zh: 当你有很多孩子时，你更希望他们中的一些人，如果不是全部的话，能离开家出去，对吧？

sentences.en: And houses have gotten bigger, too.
sentences.zh: 而且房子也变大了。

sentences.en: When you've got a small house and a bunch of kids, you don't want them all hanging around the house.
sentences.zh: 当你住在一个小房子里却有一群孩子时，你可不想让他们全都闲在家里转悠。

sentences.en: You say that another reason adults have intruded in their children's lives is that increasingly many adults feel the need to prepare children for a very competitive world.
sentences.zh: 你曾说，成年人干涉孩子生活的另一个原因是，越来越多的成年人感到有必要让孩子为竞争激烈的世界做好准备。

sentences.en: Talk about this idea, Peter.
sentences.zh: 彼得，聊聊这个想法吧。

sentences.en: Yes, I think we have become, over time, increasingly concerned about our children's competitiveness.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为随着时间的推移，我们对孩子的竞争力的关注越来越高。

sentences.en: We in the United States were a competitive culture to begin with.
sentences.zh: 我们美国本来就是一个崇尚竞争的文化。

sentences.en: And the other thing that's happened, I think, really ever since about 1980, there's been continuous growth in the gap between the rich and the poor in this country.
sentences.zh: 发生的另一件事是，我认为大约从1980年以来，这个国家贫富差距一直在持续扩大。

sentences.en: And there's actually research indicating that when the gap between rich and poor is great, parents become increasingly anxious about their children's future.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有研究表明，当贫富差距悬殊时，父母对孩子未来的焦虑感就会与日俱增。

sentences.en: Especially as the job market changes in ways that most parents don't necessarily understand and are kind of unpredictable and there's a lot of pressure on kids and creates a more competitive schooling environment than was present before.
sentences.zh: 特别是随着就业市场的变化，这种变化是大多数父母不一定能理解的，而且有点难以预测，这给孩子们带来了巨大的压力，创造了一个比以往更具竞争力的学校环境。

sentences.en: You say that there are serious consequences of depriving children of unstructured and unsupervised play.
sentences.zh: 你说过，剥夺孩子无结构、无监督的游戏会带来严重的后果。

sentences.en: What are the effects of excessive adult supervision on the social, emotional, and intellectual development of children?
sentences.zh: 过多的成人监督对儿童的社交、情感和智力发展有什么影响？

sentences.en: Over the same decades that we have been gradually decreasing children's opportunities to play independently of adults,
sentences.zh: 就在我们逐渐减少儿童独立于成年人玩耍机会的这几十年里，

sentences.en: we have seen a continuous rise in anxiety and depression and tragically even suicide among school-aged kids.
sentences.zh: 我们看到学龄儿童的焦虑、抑郁，甚至悲剧性自杀事件持续上升。

sentences.en: So, of course, that correlation doesn't by itself prove a cause-and-effect relationship, but that's the first step for believing.
sentences.zh: 所以，当然，这种相关性本身并不能证明因果关系，但这却是相信这一点的第一步。

sentences.en: Well, maybe the fact that children are not playing and exploring and doing things independently, maybe that's why they are so anxious, so depressed, so unhappy,
sentences.zh: 嗯，也许孩子们没有玩耍、探索和独立做事，也许这就是他们如此焦虑、抑郁、不快乐的原因，

sentences.en: so lacking in the resilience that we wish they would have.
sentences.zh: 缺乏我们希望他们拥有的那种复原力。

sentences.en: Now, there's both theoretical reasons and empirical reasons for believing that there is this cause-effect relationship.
sentences.zh: 现在，有理论上的原因和实证上的原因来支持这种因果关系的存在。

sentences.en: Can you tell me a little bit about that?
sentences.zh: 能跟我多讲讲这个吗？

sentences.en: What is the evidence?
sentences.zh: 证据是什么？

sentences.en: So, let me begin with just the theoretical part.
sentences.zh: 那么，我先从理论部分开始讲起。

sentences.en: Play makes children happy.
sentences.zh: 玩耍能给孩子们带来快乐。

sentences.en: We shouldn't have to prove that, right?
sentences.zh: 我们不应该非得去证明这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, play is what makes children happy.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，玩耍才是让孩子们快乐的源泉。

sentences.en: It's also the case in other kinds of independent activities.
sentences.zh: 在其他类型的独立活动中也是如此。

sentences.en: Children feel good.
sentences.zh: 孩子们感觉很好。

sentences.en: They feel proud when they can do things by themselves.
sentences.zh: 当他们能自己独立完成事情时，他们会感到自豪。

sentences.en: You know, it gives you a sense of confidence and so on.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这会给你一种自信心，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So, you take that away from children and right off, they're going to be less happy.
sentences.zh: 所以，你把这些从孩子身边拿走，马上，他们就会变得不那么快乐。

sentences.en: And a famous play researcher, Brian Sutton Smith, who died a few years ago, and he used to say,
sentences.zh: 一位几年前去世的著名游戏研究员布赖恩·萨顿·史密斯，他过去常说，

sentences.en: the opposite of play is depression.
sentences.zh: 玩耍的反义词是抑郁。

sentences.en: And I think, in a sense, he's right, that if you take away play from people, they're going to be depressed.
sentences.zh: 我想，从某种意义上说他是对的，如果你剥夺了人们玩耍的权利，他们就会抑郁。

sentences.en: But in addition to that, what research shows is that when children are playing and doing other things independently,
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，研究表明，当孩子们在玩耍和独立做其他事情时，

sentences.en: they are acquiring the skills and the sense of agency, the sense of what psychologists call an internal locus of control
sentences.zh: 他们正在获得各种技能和自主感，也就是心理学家所说的内部控制源，

sentences.en: that leads them to recognize that they can solve probleMs.
sentences.zh: 这让他们认识到自己能够解决问题。

sentences.en: They can deal with the bumps in the road of life.
sentences.zh: 他们能够应对生活道路上的坎坷。

sentences.en: You're dealing with that when you're playing.
sentences.zh: 你在玩耍时就是在应对这些。

sentences.en: You know, somebody's bullying you a little bit, and instead of a parent or an adult solving the problem,
sentences.zh: 你知道，当有人稍微欺负你一下时，不是由父母或成年人来解决问题，

sentences.en: you figure out how to solve that problem, or you get hurt and you figure out what to do about it,
sentences.zh: 而是你自己想办法解决那个问题，或者你受伤了然后弄清楚该怎么处理，

sentences.en: or you get lost and you find your way home.
sentences.zh: 或者你迷路了然后自己找到回家的路。

sentences.en: All of these are the kinds of experiences that children throughout history have always experienced,
sentences.zh: 所有这些都是历史上儿童们一直经历的种种体验，

sentences.en: and it's how they learn, I can deal with probleMs.
sentences.zh: 这也是他们学习的方式：我能够应对问题。

sentences.en: I don't have to be afraid of the world because I can solve these probleMs.
sentences.zh: 我不需要害怕这个世界，因为我能解决这些问题。

sentences.en: But if we're not allowing children to do that, they don't develop this internal sense of control.
sentences.zh: 但如果我们不允许孩子们这样做，他们就无法培养这种内在的控制感。

sentences.en: That sets you up to be anxious, and if it goes too far, it sets you up to be depressed.
sentences.zh: 这就会让你变得容易焦虑，如果发展过头，就会让你变得抑郁。

sentences.en: A sense of hopelessness about the world.
sentences.zh: 对世界产生一种绝望感。

sentences.en: So those are the theoretical reasons.
sentences.zh: 所以这些是理论上的原因。

sentences.en: The empirical reasons come from a whole range of other kinds of studies that show
sentences.zh: 实证原因来自一系列其他类型研究，这些研究表明，

sentences.en: that those children who do have more opportunity for independent play
sentences.zh: 那些拥有更多独立玩耍机会的孩子，

sentences.en: are doing better psychologically than those who have less.
sentences.zh: 在心理上的表现要比那些机会较少的好。

sentences.en: Do you think there are any positives, Peter, to the increased involvement of adults in children's lives?
sentences.zh: 彼得，你认为成年人更多地参与到儿童的生活中，有什么积极的方面吗？

sentences.en: You could point to some positive changes.
sentences.zh: 你可以指出一些积极的变化。

sentences.en: There are fewer teenage traffic accidents because fewer teenagers are driving.
sentences.zh: 少儿车祸减少了，因为开车的青少年变少了。

sentences.en: There's actually less sex among teenagers than in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 事实上，现在的青少年性行为也比过去少。

sentences.en: So historically, in many ways, we might regard it as a good thing.
sentences.zh: 所以在历史上，从很多方面来看，我们可能会认为这是一件好事。

sentences.en: There are fewer sexually transmitted diseases among young people.
sentences.zh: 年轻人中患性传播疾病的人数减少了。

sentences.en: There's fewer unwanted pregnancies and so on than in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 与过去相比，非意愿怀孕等情况减少了。

sentences.en: So some people point to those things as positive developments that have occurred
sentences.zh: 因此，有些人指出这些是积极的发展，

sentences.en: from the fact that there's much more adult involvement in children's lives.
sentences.zh: 这源于成年人更多地参与到了儿童的生活中。

sentences.en: When we come back, how to balance the imperatives of exploration and safety.
sentences.zh: 广告之后，我们将探讨如何在探索与安全的需求之间取得平衡。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹坦。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹坦。

sentences.en: Peter Gray is a psychologist at Boston College.
sentences.zh: 彼得·格雷是波士顿学院的心理学家。

sentences.en: He's the author of Free to Learn, Why Unleashing the Instinct to Play
sentences.zh: 他是《自由来学习：为什么释放玩耍的本能

sentences.en: Will Make Our Children Happier, More Self-Reliant, and Better Students for Life.
sentences.zh: 能让我们的孩子更快乐、更自立，并成为终身受益的优秀学生》一书的作者。

sentences.en: Peter, you've laid out some of the problems that arise from our present-day approach to parenting and education.
sentences.zh: 彼得，你已经列举了我们当今的育儿和教育方法所产生的一些问题。

sentences.en: You say that we can get a glimpse of what a healthier culture of childhood would look like
sentences.zh: 你说过，我们可以通过回顾过去，

sentences.en: by turning to the paSt.
sentences.zh: 一窥更健康的童年文化会是什么样子。

sentences.en: What was your own childhood like, Peter?
sentences.zh: 彼得，你自己的童年是怎样的？

sentences.en: I was a kid in the 1950s, which was a time there were a lot of kids.
sentences.zh: 我是20世纪50年代的孩子，那是一个有很多孩子的时代。

sentences.en: We moved a lot, but I found I made friends very quickly because all I had to do was to go outdoors
sentences.zh: 我们经常搬家，但我发现我很快就能交到朋友，因为我只需要走到户外，

sentences.en: and I would find other kids.
sentences.zh: 就能找到其他孩子。

sentences.en: And certainly by the time I started school, I was walking to school by myself, as was everybody else.
sentences.zh: 当然，到我上学的时候，我是自己步行去学校的，其他人也一样。

sentences.en: When Peter turned five, his family moved from Minneapolis to a small town in southern Minnesota.
sentences.zh: 彼得五岁时，他的全家从明尼阿波利斯搬到了明尼苏达州南部的一个小镇。

sentences.en: Job number one for little Peter, find new friends.
sentences.zh: 小彼得的第一项任务：找新朋友。

sentences.en: I remember my mother saying, well, why don't you just go door-to-door, knock on the doors,
sentences.zh: 我记得我母亲说，为什么你不在街区里挨家挨户敲门，

sentences.en: and ask if there are any children there your age.
sentences.zh: 问问有没有和你年龄相仿的孩子。

sentences.en: So I did that all by myself, went door-to-door, and it turns out that right across the street,
sentences.zh: 于是我自己去试了，挨家挨户地敲门，结果就在马路对面，

sentences.en: the mom came to the door, and I said, do you have any children who are about my age?
sentences.zh: 一位母亲来开门，我问她，你们家有没有跟我差不多大的孩子？

sentences.en: And she said, yes, yes, I've got a daughter, Ruby Lou.
sentences.zh: 她说，有啊，我有女儿，叫露比·娄（Ruby Lou）。

sentences.en: And so Ruby Lou came to the door, and we went out to play, and Ruby Lou very quickly became my best friend.
sentences.zh: 于是露比·娄就出来了，我们一起出去玩，很快她就成了我最好的朋友。

sentences.en: Tell me a little bit about her.
sentences.zh: 跟我多讲讲她的事吧。

sentences.en: What would you do together?
sentences.zh: 你们平时会一起做什么？

sentences.en: So Ruby Lou was a little bit older than me.
sentences.zh: 露比·娄比我大一点。

sentences.en: She started school before I did, but it was partly just the difference in when her birthday was.
sentences.zh: 她比我早入学，但部分原因也只是因为她生日在几月份。

sentences.en: And she was kind of bolder than I was.
sentences.zh: 而且她比我更大胆、更有主见。

sentences.en: I was kind of a shy kid in some ways, a little bit afraid of heights and so on.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面我算是个比较害羞的孩子，有点恐高之类的。

sentences.en: But she was a great tree climber.
sentences.zh: 但她是个爬树高手。

sentences.en: She showed me how to climb the trees, and she would challenge me to climb higher and higher in the trees.
sentences.zh: 她教我怎么爬树，还会挑衅我越爬越高。

sentences.en: I think the story that I remember best is that she had a bicycle.
sentences.zh: 我印象最深的一件事是她有一辆自行车。

sentences.en: I, at that point, did not have a bicycle, and I was really eager to learn how to ride a bicycle.
sentences.zh: 那时候我还没有自行车，我特别渴望学会骑车。

sentences.en: So she said, well, I'll teach you how to ride a bicycle.
sentences.zh: 于是她说，行吧，我来教你骑自行车。

sentences.en: So it turns out the street between our houses was on a small slope.
sentences.zh: 我们两家之间的那条街道刚好在一个小坡上。

sentences.en: And so she said, well, the easiest way to learn how to ride a bicycle is start at the top of the slope and give yourself a push.
sentences.zh: 她说，学骑车最简单的方法就是从坡顶开始，自己往前一蹬。

sentences.en: And then you just start pedaling and go as far as you can go and see if you can go a little farther every time.
sentences.zh: 然后开始踩脚踏板，能骑多远就骑多远，看看每次能不能比上一次骑得更远一点。

sentences.en: I mean, what wonderful instructions for how to ride a bicycle.
sentences.zh: 我的天，这关于怎么学骑车的指导真是太棒了。

sentences.en: And so I did that, and her bike was a girl's bike, which made it easier to learn because I didn't have to swing my leg up over that bar.
sentences.zh: 于是我就照着做了，她的车是一辆女式自行车，这让学习变得更简单了，因为我不用把腿抬得高高地跨过那根横梁。

sentences.en: And so she taught me how to ride a bicycle.
sentences.zh: 就这样她教会了我骑自行车。

sentences.en: Then once I could ride a bicycle, I convinced my parents to buy me a secondhand bike.
sentences.zh: 等我会骑车之后，我说服父母给我买了一辆二手自行车。

sentences.en: She and I would take bicycle trips all around town, and my mother said, it's fine for me.
sentences.zh: 我和她开始在全镇到处骑车兜风，我母亲说，这对我没问题。

sentences.en: I could, by myself, I had to stay within the town limits on the bike.
sentences.zh: 我可以独自骑车，但必须在镇子规定的范围内。

sentences.en: But with Ruby Lou, it would be okay to go wherever we wanted because she assumed Ruby Lou was wiser and a little older and smarter than I was.
sentences.zh: 但如果是和露比·娄一起，去哪儿都行，因为她觉得露比·娄比我更懂事、大一点也更聪明。

sentences.en: I think she was.
sentences.zh: 我觉得她确实是那样。

sentences.en: And we could go places together.
sentences.zh: 我们俩可以一起去很多地方。

sentences.en: I understand you played a lot of sports, but these were not like the adult-organized sports teams that we have today.
sentences.zh: 我听说你以前玩过很多运动，但这些可不是我们今天看到的那些由成人组织的运动队。

sentences.en: Yeah, so the kids were all into baseball there, and we would just get together whenever we could on the vacant lot, whatever kids were around,
sentences.zh: 对，那会儿孩子们都迷棒球，只要有机会大家就会聚在空地上，不管当时有哪些孩子在场，

sentences.en: and we'd create our own baseball games.
sentences.zh: 我们自己就能组织一场棒球赛。

sentences.en: And so each team had to sort of choose their own player who would kind of be the coach, who would decide who's going to play what positions and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 所以每支队伍都得选出自己的队员来当教练，由他来决定谁打什么位置之类的。

sentences.en: And for some reason, even though I was one of the youngest players, the players chose me on my team to be the coach.
sentences.zh: 不知为什么，尽管我是年纪最小的队员之一，我队里的成员还是选了我当教练。

sentences.en: So that meant that I was the one who had to remind people when the games were.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我要负责提醒大家比赛的时间。

sentences.en: I had to decide who was going to pitch.
sentences.zh: 我还得决定谁来投球。

sentences.en: Everybody wanted to pitch.
sentences.zh: 每个人都想投球。

sentences.en: So I had to figure out some rotating way to please everybody.
sentences.zh: 所以我必须想出一个轮流的办法来让大家都满意。

sentences.en: I mean, the biggest challenge, of course, you have in a situation like this is you want everybody to stay on the team.
sentences.zh: 当然，这种情况下你面临的最大挑战就是，你希望每个人都留在队里。

sentences.en: You want to keep everybody happy.
sentences.zh: 你想让所有人都开心。

sentences.en: And it was kind of very much an adult-like responsibility to manage this team when I was – I suppose I would have been about eight years old at that time.
sentences.zh: 管理这支队伍真是一种极具成人感的责任，当时我——我想我那时候大概八岁左右吧。

sentences.en: But there were no adults.
sentences.zh: 但周围没有大人。

sentences.en: Adults never came to these games.
sentences.zh: 大人们从不参与这些比赛。

sentences.en: You know, the only adult involved was – it probably was a teenager who would be an umpire there, who would call balls and strikes and fair and foul.
sentences.zh: 你知道，唯一参与的大人——那可能也就是个青少年，在场上当裁判，负责判定好球、坏球、界内球和界外球。

sentences.en: And that's what made it different from our pickup games.
sentences.zh: 这就是它跟我们自发野球的不同之处。

sentences.en: I mean, it would be hard to imagine an eight- or nine-year-old in charge of a little league baseball team today.
sentences.zh: 说实话，很难想象现在会让一个八九岁的孩子去掌管一支少儿棒球联盟的球队。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: This is a change in our expectations.
sentences.zh: 这是我们期望值的改变。

sentences.en: It's not a change in what people are capable of biologically.
sentences.zh: 并不是人们的生物学能力发生了变化。

sentences.en: But it's in other cultures, in Huster-Gather cultures, you would not be surprised by something like this, that an eight-year-old could take that kind of responsibility.
sentences.zh: 但在其他文化中，比如狩猎采集文化中，你对这种事就不会感到惊讶，一个八岁的孩子完全能承担起那种责任。

sentences.en: Now, clearly it was a different time, a different era.
sentences.zh: 现在很明显，那是不同的时代，不同的纪元。

sentences.en: But you have some suggestions on how we might bring back an element of playfulness into children's lives in our present day.
sentences.zh: 但你对我们如何在当下把游戏精神重新融入孩子的生活提出了一些建议。

sentences.en: And you say that parents can ask a simple question to their children that could get the ball rolling.
sentences.zh: 你说父母可以向孩子问一个简单的问题来打开局面。

sentences.en: What is this question, Peter?
sentences.zh: 彼得，这个问题是什么？

sentences.en: What is something that you really would like to do, that you feel you could do, but you'd like to do on your own?
sentences.zh: 有什么事情是你真的很想做、觉得自己能做到、但又想自己一个人独立完成的？

sentences.en: And initiate that conversation.
sentences.zh: 然后开启这段对话。

sentences.en: See what the child says.
sentences.zh: 看看孩子怎么说。

sentences.en: And maybe the child will say, well, you know, I'd like to be able to ride my bicycle all by myself to my friend's house.
sentences.zh: 也许孩子会说，你知道的，我想自己一个人骑自行车去朋友家。

sentences.en: Or maybe the child will say, I'd actually like to cook dinner.
sentences.zh: 或者孩子会说，我其实想自己做顿晚饭。

sentences.en: But now the child is asked and the parent is having this discussion.
sentences.zh: 但现在孩子被问到了，父母也正在进行这样的讨论。

sentences.en: And the idea would be to reach some kind of a kind of a agreement.
sentences.zh: 核心的想法是达成某种共识或协议。

sentences.en: Well, OK, you can do this.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你可以做这个。

sentences.en: And it may not be exactly what the child's asking for, but something that the parent is thinks is OK.
sentences.zh: 这可能不完全是孩子要求的那个，但会是父母觉得没问题的事情。

sentences.en: So that kind of breaks into this cycle where you sort of change the discussion.
sentences.zh: 所以这打破了那种旧的循环，改变了讨论的方向。

sentences.en: It's not now just about safety.
sentences.zh: 重点不再仅仅是安全。

sentences.en: It's now about balancing safety with an acknowledged value in independent activity and an acknowledgement that what the child wants to do is actually important.
sentences.zh: 现在变成了在安全与独立活动中公认的价值之间寻找平衡，并且承认孩子想做的事情其实很重要。

sentences.en: You say that parents can also work with other like-minded adults to make space and time for lightly supervised play.
sentences.zh: 你说父母也可以和其他志同道合的成年人合作，为轻度监管的游戏腾出空间和时间。

sentences.en: How would this work?
sentences.zh: 这具体该怎么做？

sentences.en: This has actually occurred in some neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 这其实已经在一些社区发生过了。

sentences.en: I wish it occurred more.
sentences.zh: 我希望这种现象能更多一些。

sentences.en: Where some parent or maybe more than one parent have decided, you know, we really would like our children to have more opportunities to play without us intervening.
sentences.zh: 有些父母，或者不止一位父母决定，你知道的，我们真的很想给孩子们更多不需要我们介入就能玩耍的机会。

sentences.en: We remember our own experiences as children and what we benefited from play.
sentences.zh: 我们记起自己小时候的经历以及从游戏中获得了多少益处。

sentences.en: We need to provide this for our children.
sentences.zh: 我们需要为我们的孩子提供这一点。

sentences.en: How can we do it?
sentences.zh: 我们该怎么做？

sentences.en: And so one strategy is to get together with the neighbors who have kids and you say, all right, every Saturday, we're all going to send our kids out and keep your devices inside.
sentences.zh: 所以其中一个策略就是和有孩子的邻居们聚在一起，你们说，好了，每个星期六，我们都要把孩子赶出去，把电子设备留在家里。

sentences.en: We're going to send you out.
sentences.zh: 我们这就让你们出去。

sentences.en: But they're all going out.
sentences.zh: 但他们全都是一起出去。

sentences.en: If some of the parents are concerned about safety, we'll have one adult out there just for safety.
sentences.zh: 如果有些父母担心安全问题，我们可以只派一个成年人在外面负责安全。

sentences.en: In my opinion, ideally, that adult is a grandparent because I find that grandparents tend to be a little less likely to intervene than parents are.
sentences.zh: 依我之见，理想情况下，这个成年人最好是祖父母，因为我发现祖父母往往比父母更不容易插手干预。

sentences.en: But the understanding would be that that adult is like a lifeguard on an ocean beach, only there in case there's some kind of real danger.
sentences.zh: 但大家的共识是，那个成年人就像海滩上的救生员，只有在发生某种真正的危险时才会出面。

sentences.en: But not to tell the children how to play or to solve minor probleMs.
sentences.zh: 而不是去告诉孩子们该怎么玩，或者帮他们解决小问题。

sentences.en: And so there are a few neighborhoods who have done that, including some that have actually got the city to close off the streets, if it's a busy street,
sentences.zh: 所以确实有一些社区这样做了，其中包括一些甚至成功让市政府在游戏时间封闭街道的做法，如果那是条繁忙的街道的话。

sentences.en: during that period of time when it's playtime.
sentences.zh: 在这段玩耍的时间里。

sentences.en: And once the kids are playing together and they get to know one another, then they may find other ways to play during other times as well, other than just the formally chosen one.
sentences.zh: 一旦孩子们开始一起玩并逐渐熟悉彼此，他们可能会在除了这种正式选定的时间之外，也找到其他方式来一起玩耍。

sentences.en: Peter says schools can also play a role in promoting play.
sentences.zh: 彼得说学校也可以在促进游戏方面发挥作用。

sentences.en: He has been working with schools around the country to create play clubs.
sentences.zh: 他一直在与全国各地的学校合作创建游戏俱乐部。

sentences.en: And what play club is, is an hour of free age-mixed play, usually in elementary schools, all the grades combined.
sentences.zh: 所谓的游戏俱乐部，就是一个小时的自由、混龄游戏，通常在小学里进行，所有年级混在一起。

sentences.en: So it's age 5 through 11, roughly, all combined, all playing together.
sentences.zh: 所以大概是从5岁到11岁左右，所有人混在一起玩。

sentences.en: Usually it is before school, but sometimes after school.
sentences.zh: 通常是在上学前，但有时也在放学后。

sentences.en: And so this takes a little bit of effort on the part of the school.
sentences.zh: 所以这需要学校付出一点点努力。

sentences.en: They have to have somebody there to manage it.
sentences.zh: 他们必须派个人去管理现场。

sentences.en: And the teachers who monitor play club are advised, taught, really, not to solve little quarrels, not to tell the children how to play better,
sentences.zh: 监督游戏俱乐部的老师们会得到建议，或者说培训，不要去解决小争执，不要告诉孩子们如何玩得更好，

sentences.en: not to worry if somebody looks unhappy.
sentences.zh: 如果有人看起来不高兴，也不用大惊小怪。

sentences.en: The whole purpose of play is for children to learn how to solve their own probleMs.
sentences.zh: 游戏的核心目的就是为了让孩子们学会如何解决自己的问题。

sentences.en: For the schools that have adopted this, this has been very successful.
sentences.zh: 对于采纳了这个做法的学校来说，这非常成功。

sentences.en: So, Peter, you say that much of this boils down to a question of trust, to the willingness that adults have to trust their children, that left to their own devices,
sentences.zh: 所以，彼得，你说这在很大程度上归结为一个信任问题，即成年人是否愿意信任自己的孩子——相信在放任他们自己去支配时间的情况下，

sentences.en: they're going to spend their time in positive and productive ways.
sentences.zh: 他们会以积极和富有成效的方式度过时光。

sentences.en: Can you talk about this idea that, at its core, there's an emotional element here, that if parents actually trusted their kids to do the smart thing and to do the right thing,
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这个核心观点吗？这里面存在一个情感因素，如果父母真的信任自己的孩子能做出明智和正确的事情，

sentences.en: they might be less interested in engaging or intervening constantly in their children's lives?
sentences.zh: 他们可能就不会那么热衷于不断介入或干涉孩子的生活了？

sentences.en: Really, what we're talking about here is to what degree do you as a parent feel that you need to control your child?
sentences.zh: 真的，我们在这里讨论的是，作为父母，你在多大程度上觉得自己需要控制孩子？

sentences.en: And to what degree do you feel you can trust your child to do what is good for the child themselves without you controlling?
sentences.zh: 以及在多大程度上你觉得自己可以信任孩子，相信他们在没有你控制的情况下也能做出对他们自身有利的事情？

sentences.en: So, really, ultimately, what I mean by a trustful parent is one who trusts the child's developmental processes and allows those developmental processes to occur,
sentences.zh: 所以归根结底，我所说的信任型父母，是指那些信任孩子自身发展过程并允许这些过程自然发生的人，

sentences.en: which really means allowing the child to play, to explore, ask questions of adults when they want to ask those questions and all of that,
sentences.zh: 这实际上意味着允许孩子去玩耍、去探索、在想问成年人问题时去提问，诸如此类，

sentences.en: to do the things that children by nature want to do.
sentences.zh: 去完成孩子们天性中就想做的事情。

sentences.en: In your work, you recount a remarkable story that is a kind of real-life version of the novel, Lord of the Flies.
sentences.zh: 在你的工作中，你讲述了一个非同寻常的故事，它堪称小说《蝇王》的现实生活版。

sentences.en: The story was unearthed by a Dutch historian, Rutger Bregman.
sentences.zh: 这个故事是由一位荷兰历史学家鲁特格尔·布雷格曼（Rutger Bregman）发掘出来的。

sentences.en: Tell me that story.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲那个故事吧。

sentences.en: There was a real case in the 1960s of a group of schoolboys, about the same age as the fictitious children in Lord of the Flies, living on a Pacific island.
sentences.zh: 那是20世纪60年代的一个真实案例，一群男学生，年龄和《蝇王》里虚构的孩子差不多，居住在一个太平洋岛屿上。

sentences.en: They ranged in age from 13 to 16, and they had decided they were tired of school.
sentences.zh: 他们的年龄在13到16岁之间，当时他们觉得厌学了。

sentences.en: They were at a boarding school, and they called it borrowing, but they basically stole a fishing boat.
sentences.zh: 他们在寄宿学校上学，他们美其名曰借，但基本上是偷了一艘渔船。

sentences.en: And they weren't really very good sailors, so they went off into the ocean, aimed at another island that they wanted to get to.
sentences.zh: 而且他们其实并不太会开船，所以他们驶向大海，目标是他们想去的另一个岛屿。

sentences.en: But a big storm came up, and they ended up shipwrecked on an uninhabited island, and nobody found them for 15 months.
sentences.zh: 但一场大风暴袭来，导致他们在一座无人岛上遭遇海难，15个月里没有人找到他们。

sentences.en: Unlike in Lord of the Flies, these kids took care of themselves.
sentences.zh: 和《蝇王》里不同，这些孩子照顾好了自己。

sentences.en: They did not war with one another.
sentences.zh: 他们没有互相打仗。

sentences.en: They recognized, you know, our lives are in danger here.
sentences.zh: 他们意识到，我们的生命在这里受到了威胁。

sentences.en: They figured out how to find food.
sentences.zh: 他们想办法寻找食物。

sentences.en: They figured out what's edible, what's not edible.
sentences.zh: 他们弄清楚了什么能吃，什么不能吃。

sentences.en: They actually planted a garden.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至种了个菜园。

sentences.en: They created a garden in case they were there for a long time.
sentences.zh: 他们开辟了一个菜园，以防在那里呆很长时间。

sentences.en: They always had one child on watch for passing ships to try to flag them.
sentences.zh: 他们总是安排一个孩子放哨，留意过往的船只，试图向它们发出信号。

sentences.en: One of the boys broke a leg, and the kids figured out how to set the leg to protect it, and it actually healed up.
sentences.zh: 其中一个男孩摔断了腿，孩子们想办法把腿固定好以进行保护，最后它竟然真的愈合了。

sentences.en: They took care of one another in a remarkable way.
sentences.zh: 他们以一种非凡的方式照顾彼此。

sentences.en: They survived, and so this is a story that's the exact opposite of the fiction Lord of the Flies.
sentences.zh: 他们活了下来，所以这是一个与虚构的《蝇王》截然相反的故事。

sentences.en: Peter Gray is a psychologist at Boston College.
sentences.zh: 彼得·格雷是波士顿学院的心理学家。

sentences.en: He's the author of Free to Learn, Why Unleashing the Instinct to Play Will Make Our Children Happier, More Self-Reliant, and Better Students for Life.
sentences.zh: 他是《自由学习：释放游戏本能如何让我们的孩子更快乐、更自主、一生受益》一书的作者。

sentences.en: Peter, thank you for joining me today on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 彼得，谢谢你今天来到《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: Thank you very much for having me on.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来参加。

sentences.en: Do you have follow-up questions for Peter Gray about children, play, and independence?
sentences.zh: 你对彼得·格雷关于儿童、游戏和独立性的问题有什么后续想法吗？

sentences.zh: 如果你愿意与《隐藏的大脑》听众分享你的问题，请录制一段语音备忘录并发送给我们，邮箱是 ideas@hiddenbrain.org。

sentences.zh: 再重复一遍邮箱地址是 ideas@hiddenbrain.org。

sentences.zh: 主题行请写：play。

sentences.en: We end today with a story from our sister podcast, My Unsung Hero.
sentences.zh: 节目最后，我们带来姊妹播客《我无名英雄》里的一个故事。

sentences.en: It's brought to you by T-Mobile for Business.
sentences.zh: 本节目由 T-Mobile 企业版为您赞助播出。

sentences.en: Our story comes from River Adams, who uses they, them pronouns.
sentences.zh: 我们的故事来自里弗·亚当斯（River Adams），他们的代词是 they/them。

sentences.en: In 1991, at the age of 19, River and their family came to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 1991年，19岁的里弗和家人作为来自苏联的犹太难民来到美国。

sentences.en: as Jewish refugees from the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 作为来自苏联的犹太难民来到美国。

sentences.en: Though the family received a small amount of support from welfare and food stamps, it wasn't nearly enough to survive on.
sentences.zh: 虽然这家人从福利救济和食品券中得到了一点支持，但这远远不足以维生。

sentences.en: So River and their older sister tried to apply for jobs, but neither spoke much English.
sentences.zh: 因此里弗和他们的姐姐试图申请工作，但两人都不会说太多英语。

sentences.en: For the first several months, no one would hire us because, well, we couldn't pass an interview.
sentences.zh: 头几个月，没人愿意雇佣我们，因为，嗯，我们根本通不过面试。

sentences.en: We didn't even understand the simple questions the employers were asking.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至听不懂雇主问的那些简单问题。

sentences.en: So the four of us were always hungry.
sentences.zh: 所以我们四个人总是饿肚子。

sentences.en: Our diet consisted almost entirely of macaroni with ketchup, discounted manager's special bananas, and the cheapest cereal we could find, which was Froot Loops.
sentences.zh: 我们的日常饮食几乎全是由加番茄酱的通心粉、超市经理特价打折的香蕉，以及我们能找到的最便宜的麦片（也就是彩色圈圈麦片）组成的。

sentences.en: But, you know, still there was never enough of these foods either.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，这些食物依然从来都不够吃。

sentences.en: Then in the summer of 91, my sister and I were hired to work at Roy Rogers.
sentences.zh: 然后在91年夏天，我和姐姐被罗伊·罗杰斯（Roy Rogers）录用了。

sentences.en: It was a fast food chain that was very common then, and they specialized in fried chicken.
sentences.zh: 那是当时很常见的一家快餐连锁店，他们的招牌是炸鸡。

sentences.en: And the manager who hired us, he did us a kindness just by giving us the job, because we were still, you know, really not with it.
sentences.zh: 雇用我们的经理，他给我们这份工作本身就是一种恩惠，因为我们当时，你知道的，确实状态很不在线。

sentences.en: And all I remember about this man is that his name was Ed.
sentences.zh: 我关于这个人唯一的记忆就是他叫埃德。

sentences.en: So the work was hard, but being hungry and surrounded by all this food was harder.
sentences.zh: 所以工作很苦，但忍受饥饿还要被所有这些食物包围则更苦。

sentences.en: We couldn't afford any of it.
sentences.zh: 我们什么也买不起。

sentences.en: When other workers bought their meals during breaks, we didn't eat.
sentences.zh: 当其他工人在休息时间买饭时，我们不吃。

sentences.en: And I think after a while, Ed realized the financial situation we were in, and he began to help us.
sentences.zh: 我想过了一段时间后，埃德意识到了我们的财务状况，他开始帮助我们。

sentences.en: We worked the evening shift, so after we would close and clean the restaurant, Ed would put the leftover fried chicken into a bucket and give it to us to take home to our family.
sentences.zh: 我们上的是晚班，所以在我们打烊并打扫完餐厅后，埃德会把剩下的炸鸡装进一个桶里，给我们带回家给家人吃。

sentences.en: And for the first time in months, the four of us ate, we didn't go to sleep hungry, and suddenly we had hope that we would survive.
sentences.zh: 几个月来我们四个人第一次吃饱了饭，没有饿着肚子入睡，刹那间我们燃起了能够活下去的希望。

sentences.en: Of course, we didn't understand then that Ed was breaking the rules by giving us this food.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们当时并不明白埃德给我们这些食物是违背规定的。

sentences.en: I doubt that Ed remembers us, but he is a hero in our family, and we mention his name often and with utmost warmth.
sentences.zh: 我怀疑埃德还记不记得我们，但他却是我们家的英雄，我们经常提起他的名字，并且满怀温情。

sentences.en: I doubt he knows that these two new immigrants that he once hired and fed remember him as the first American who was kind to us.
sentences.zh: 我怀疑他并不知道，他曾经雇用并接济过的这两个新移民，把视为对我们好的第一个美国人。

sentences.en: He's the man who saved us.
sentences.zh: 他就是拯救了我们的人。

sentences.en: Listener River Adams of Marlboro, Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 听众马萨诸塞州马尔伯勒的里弗·亚当斯。

sentences.en: River went on to become a pianist, medical interpreter, and author.
sentences.zh: 里弗后来成为了一名钢琴家、医疗口译员和作家。

sentences.zh: 今天的《我叫桑吉拉的姑妈》故事由 T-Mobile 企业版为您呈现。

sentences.en: Thanks for listening.
sentences.zh: 谢谢收听。

sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.zh: 回头见。
